Subject: Request: Admin roles, SCIM sync architecture and evidence

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move through our vendor security review, the InfoSec and Identity teams have a few concrete deliverables we need to validate for the RFP. I attached our spreadsheet with numbered questions, but the high-priority items are below so we can align on follow-ups:

1) Admin/RBAC matrix: we need a CSV or table that maps built-in roles, their capabilities (user create, deactivate, group management, API access, audit access) and whether roles are configurable by customers.

2) SCIM provisioning architecture: a short diagram and description of how SCIM syncs groups/users (SCIM 2.0), paging behavior for large orgs, handling of partial updates, conflict resolution when downstream changes are made, and typical sync latency for 10k-100k users.

3) SSO mapping notes: what attributes you require for SAML and OIDC (email, externalId, groups), and whether multiple IdPs / IdP-initiated SSO is supported per organization.

4) Audit and retention: what audit logs are available for user lifecycle and admin actions, retention windows, and export capability for security review.

5) Evidence: sample SCIM request/response (sanitized), an admin roles CSV, and any diagram you can share.

We aim to close the identity section by Friday 24th. Can you confirm owners and a delivery plan? If helpful, we can schedule a short technical call with our identity engineer.

Thanks,
Asha Mehta
Lead, Vendor Security
BridgePoint Financial Services

Hi Asha — attaching the artifacts you requested and a short summary below. Thanks for the patience while we assembled everything. If you'd like, we can run through the items in a 30-min technical call — proposed times on Fri 04/23 08:00 or 11:00 PDT.

Summary answers (short):
1) Admin/RBAC matrix: attached admin-roles-matrix.csv. We ship a set of built-in roles (Org Admin, Billing Admin, Support Admin, Developer, Read-Only) and customers can create custom roles on Enterprise plans. The CSV maps each role to capabilities (create/deactivate users, group management, API keys, view/export audit). Notes column flags features that require Dedicated/Private deployments.

2) SCIM provisioning architecture: attached scim-architecture-diagram.png and redwood-scim-sample.json. We implement SCIM 2.0 (PATCH/PUT/POST/DELETE) with support for pagination (startIndex/count) and RFC 7644 list operations. For large tenants we recommend incremental syncs combined with a periodic full reconciliation; typical incremental sync latency is sub-60s for incremental updates under normal load, full recon for 100k users completes within 20–40 minutes depending on provisioning rate and configured batching. Conflict resolution defaults to last-writer-wins; locking/ownership flags are available via attributes for customers that require stronger guarantees.

3) SAML/OIDC mapping: required attributes: userName (preferred email), externalId (optional but recommended), displayName, emails, groups. We support multiple IdPs per org and both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. OIDC flows support standard claims mapping and custom attribute mapping via the admin console.

4) Audit and retention: audit logs include user lifecycle events (create/update/deactivate), admin actions (role changes, API key generation), and SCIM sync results. Default retention 90 days; Enterprise add-on extends retention to 12 months and we can provide exports via CSV or our Audit API. Logs include timestamps, actor (user/api key), IP, and before/after state for admin changes.

Attached files: redwood-scim-sample.json, admin-roles-matrix.csv, scim-architecture-diagram.png

If you'd like us to redact anything further from the sample payloads, tell us which attributes and we'll resubmit. Otherwise, when is a good time for the tech sync?
